contexts.description: Public-facing /about route that introduces KandiDate's value proposition to prospective users with a marketing tone. It is a thin Next.js route shell that sets page metadata and Open Graph tags, then delegates all rendering to the shared Spark-art-direction AboutHome component. Opting out of Cache Components prerendering (instant=false) avoids a skeleton flash because the parent layout already runs dynamically.
contexts.name: about-page

contexts.description: UI components that manage the user experience during and around AI analysis runs. `AnalysisProgress` displays a real-time three-phase progress panel (reading, analyzing, saving) with an elapsed timer, per-variant count, and cancel affordance — shown during live CV analysis. `ScanAnimation` is an inline animated SVG (scan line + tracer dot) used as the visual loading state. `AiDisclosure` is a jurisdiction-aware candidate-facing AI transparency notice that fetches the active compliance regime and names the correct anti-discrimination framework and data law.
contexts.name: ai-analysis-ux

contexts.description: Orchestrates the end-to-end AI analysis run: phase sequencing (analyze-phases), running a recruiter-perspective analysis pass, completeness follow-up for under-specified CVs, and settling the final analysis record. Provenance dossier captures the full input-output chain for later audit or re-analysis.
contexts.name: analysis-pipeline-run

contexts.api_surface: Pure scoring helpers consumed by analysis run and screening wave
contexts.description: The core scoring engine: multi-factor match scoring (experience, skills, role seniority, education, traits → 100-point total), fit thresholds, score distribution statistics, adverse-impact detection, archetype classification (early-career vs senior vs specialist), and comparison between analysis variants.
contexts.name: analysis-scoring

contexts.description: Panels and components for AI scoring calibration: score-band distributions, per-family fit-floor chips, score drift over time, threshold suggestion, threshold change history, and the overall calibration dashboard. Recruiters use this surface to tune the match-score thresholds applied across the candidate pool. Includes the unit test for the family apply-gate logic.
contexts.name: analytics-calibration

contexts.description: Panels tracking recruitment channel economics and AI compute cost-per-hire. ChannelEconomicsPanel shows spend, hires, and cost-per-hire by channel plus JD variant recommendations; ChannelSpendInput handles inline spend editing; ComputeCostPanel reports LLM API costs from the usage ledger; OrgBenchmarkPanel benchmarks workspace metrics against the broader organisation. All panels run their own fetches independent of the main analytics payload.
contexts.name: analytics-channel-roi

contexts.description: The top-level Analytics tab that orchestrates data fetching and deferred rendering of all analytics panels. It fetches from /api/analytics with a user-selectable 30/90/all-time cohort window held in the URL, then fans out into deferred sub-panels so the funnel paints first and heavy tables mount on scroll. Also provides barrel re-exports for DeltaChip and InlineNumberSave so other modules can import from this stable entry point.
contexts.name: analytics-core-tab

contexts.description: Paginated, filterable audit log of every hiring decision made in the system, surfaced as a lazy-loaded section at the bottom of the Analytics tab. Uses infinite scroll to load decision records from /api/analytics/decisions, with a toolbar for date-range and type filters and a footer showing load status. Types and row-level renderers are colocated so the log data shape, display, and pagination live together.
contexts.name: analytics-decision-log

contexts.description: Panels covering the recruitment funnel visualization, hiring forecast, automation impact, source attribution, and offer-leg conversion analytics. Each panel is driven by the Analytics payload fetched in the core tab and renders stage-by-stage throughput, conversion rates, time-to-hire forecasts, and where candidates originate. Empty/first-run states are colocated so the funnel surface degrades gracefully before any data lands.
contexts.name: analytics-funnel-forecast

contexts.description: Shared UI primitives and breakdown panels consumed across the Analytics tab: Stat/StatCluster for labelled metric tiles, DeltaChip for period-over-period delta badges, InlineNumberSave for editable inline targets, TargetInput and GoalsEditor for recruiter-set conversion goals, plus the ByRoleTable, MomentumPanel, ArchetypePanel, and shared empty-state components. These are pure presentational building blocks with no own data fetches.
contexts.name: analytics-metrics-widgets

contexts.description: Handles all routes by which CV and supporting files enter the analyze form — drag-and-drop zone, file-picker acceptance, global drag highlight, profile-input multi-file list, and the drop-routing logic that dispatches dropped files to the right slot (CV vs JD vs company). Gate logic validates file constraints before they reach the pipeline. Feeds file arrays into the run-pipeline context.
contexts.name: analyze-file-intake

contexts.description: The History tab within the Analyze tool — displays a filterable, paginated table of past analysis runs so recruiters can revisit and reuse results. HistoryFilterBar drives filter state (date range, status, JD), HistoryTable renders the rows, and HistoryTypes defines the shared data shape. Consumes the analyses listing API and links out to individual analysis detail.
contexts.name: analyze-history

contexts.description: Implements the CV analysis execution pipeline — submitting files to the API, streaming stage-progress events, parsing the result schema, and resolving GitHub run policy. AnalyzeApi wraps the HTTP transport and error normalization; analyzeRunAnalysis orchestrates stages and maps failures to localizable error codes; analyzePipelineRef and analyzeCollapse manage the stable reference and collapse animation contract.
contexts.name: analyze-run-pipeline

contexts.description: The top-level CV analysis workspace that recruits and orchestrates the full analyze flow — tab entry point, form layout, column rendering, JD library picker, optional columns, paste row, and collapsed state. It composes the file-intake and run-pipeline sub-contexts and owns the overall visual structure of the Analyze tool. Key dependency is AnalyzeWorkspace + AnalyzeTab wiring form state into progress and results.
contexts.name: analyze-workspace-ui

contexts.description: Candidate self-service portal: token-gated status page showing application progress, pipeline stage, and any decisions. The offer route surfaces a token-gated employment offer for candidates to accept. Both routes expose zero internal IDs or scores — only candidate-safe projections.
contexts.name: application-status

contexts.description: Public, token-gated page that lets candidates check their own application status without contacting the recruiter. It polls /api/status/[token] on a 45-second interval (plus focus/visibility revalidation) and renders a 5-step timeline (received → under review → interview → offer → hired), terminal-state cards, and an Art. 86 GDPR-compliant redacted decision history fetched from /api/status/[token]/decisions. Depends on the application-status and status-decisions lib modules for status typing/classification, and on shared UI primitives (AiDisclosure, LanguageSwitcher, RouteLoading).
contexts.name: application-status-page

contexts.description: Source-contract tests that pin the candidate-facing apply surfaces against regressions that a DOM renderer cannot catch — draft fingerprint correctness, tonal neutrality of knockout buttons, decline recoverability, quick-form submit liveness, honeypot presence, and status-link wiring across both conversational and quick-apply flows. Tests use Node's built-in test runner and read the component source as text to assert structural invariants that would silently break in a restyle or refactor.
contexts.name: apply-surface-tests

contexts.description: Routes a candidate to BAU / Student-early-career / Career-switcher archetype, which determines intake form, scoring weights, and reasoning lens. Detection rules, labels, scoring weights, and dimension labels all live in the shared archetypes.json registry read by both Python and TypeScript, making archetype drift structurally impossible. registry.py is the Python view of that data.
contexts.name: archetype-detection

contexts.description: Lets recruiters define and manage candidate archetypes — the taxonomy used to classify profiles during analysis. ArchetypeManagerList renders the saved archetypes; ArchetypeManagerEditPanel handles create/edit; ArchetypeManagerViewPanel shows the detail; useArchetypeManagerActions dispatches create/update/delete. Archetypes are referenced by the profile editor and feed the candidate matrix grouping.
contexts.name: archetype-manager

contexts.description: Renders the system's committed PlantUML architecture diagrams live from disk at `/diagrams`, including an interactive pipeline-funnel explorer that opens a per-step implementation drawer. The page reads `docs/diagrams/*.puml` server-side via a module-scoped cache (`readDiagramSource`) so the display always reflects the committed source. The interactive `PipelineExplorer` maps each clickable funnel node to a `STEP_DETAILS` entry describing the wiring (UI module, API route, DB tables) and renders a mini component diagram inside a non-modal slide-in drawer.
contexts.name: architecture-diagrams-explorer

contexts.description: CI contract tests that keep the interactive architecture explorer honest: they verify every `STEP_DETAILS.files[]` entry resolves to a real path on disk, that every clickable funnel node alias in the `.puml` source has a matching drawer entry and vice versa, and that every `/api/…` route drawn in a step body maps to a real App-Router `route.ts`. A separate suite guards that `readDiagramSource` returns valid PlantUML content for every diagram the page renders and that the path resolver produces the layout the standalone Docker image expects.
contexts.name: architecture-diagrams-tests

contexts.api_surface: Outbound POST to ATS webhook URL on offer-accept
contexts.description: Outbound ATS integration (Recruitis, Teamio, and generic webhook targets): delivers accepted candidates to the external ATS at the offer-accept moment, guards delivery with idempotency and at-rest encryption for the stored ATS credentials, and records the delivery attempt status. The offer-select filter decides which offers qualify for ATS pushback.
contexts.name: ats-egress

contexts.description: External ATS push/pull bridge: configure which ATS provider is active, test connectivity, receive or push candidate records (the candidate route handles bidirectional sync with an audit trail), and list ATS delivery receipts. Auth tests verify that ATS routes reject unauthenticated callers regardless of the provider configured.
contexts.name: ats-integration

contexts.description: Tracks per-workspace attention badges (unseen activity counts) and background task queue for long-running operations. Tasks are deduplicated to prevent double-running, have a maintenance sweep to clear stale entries, and feed the task-view component that shows progress in the sidebar.
contexts.name: attention-tasks

contexts.description: Implements the request-time access guards: edge JWT verification for middleware, rate-limited login throttle, home-gate redirect logic for authenticated users, onboarding gate that forces new tenants through setup, and a public-routes allowlist. These are the entry-point guards before any feature code runs.
contexts.name: auth-gates

contexts.api_surface: Pure helpers imported by route handlers
contexts.description: Defines the five-tier membership role model (owner, admin, recruiter, hiring_manager, viewer) with a capability map that API routes gate on. Provides pure helper functions for role ranking and capability checking, plus password hashing and the require-operator guard for sensitive operations.
contexts.name: auth-rbac

contexts.api_surface: Server-side session read via Iron Session cookie
contexts.description: Manages user session lifecycle: reading the current authenticated user and workspace from Iron Session, navigating between auth states, and resolving the current workspace context server-side. Acts as the primary runtime identity source for all server components and API routes.
contexts.name: auth-session

contexts.description: Session-based authentication: login with per-account and per-IP brute-force throttling (constant-time password compare, 15-min sliding windows), logout (cookie clear), and workspace switching. The rate-limit-contract test pins the contract between client IP extraction and the throttle store.
contexts.name: authentication

contexts.description: ROI and fairness analytics for the automation layer: computes time and cost savings from automated screening decisions, measures auto-reject fairness across demographic groups (adverse-impact rates), split-ad campaign performance comparison, and automation event cache key management.
contexts.name: automation-analytics

contexts.description: The AI-driven screening wave that auto-rejects the bottom cohort percent below a match threshold while preserving fairness: never auto-rejecting early-career or unscored candidates. The holdout mechanism samples a random percentage for human review. Approval tokens gate the wave behind a human sign-off before mass-reject commits.
contexts.name: automation-engine

contexts.description: Human oversight dashboard for the autonomous hiring pipeline, providing a kill switch to pause/resume automation, a list of pending Art. 22 human gates awaiting approval, an immutable audit trail of all automated decisions, and an outcomes-and-calibration panel that records real hire/reject results and adjusts the promote-floor threshold. Polls /api/devcase/control and /api/devcase/outcomes every 3 s and routes consequential actions (approve gate, apply floor, reconcile) through the two-step arm/confirm guard in controlRoomConfirm.ts.
contexts.name: autonomy-control-room

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST /api/tasks, GET/DELETE /api/tasks/[id], POST /api/tasks/[id]/retry, GET /api/tasks/history, POST /api/automation/[task], POST /api/automation/run, GET/PUT /api/automation/schedule
contexts.description: Async task queue for long-running AI work: list active and recent tasks, start a named task (analyze, group_eval, outreach, etc.), retry failed tasks, and page through task history. The automation sub-routes trigger task pipelines from the scheduler or on demand, and the schedule endpoint configures recurring automation runs.
contexts.name: background-tasks

contexts.description: The React context layer and core logic for the workspace's background task system. TasksProvider polls /api/tasks every 2 s (signature-diffed to avoid spurious re-renders), exposes startTask/cancelTask, and re-exports useTaskResult for components that need to fetch a finished task's output. tasksTaskMeter computes UI progress metrics from raw task state.
contexts.name: background-tasks-provider

contexts.description: The full Tasks panel UI reachable from the sidebar footer indicator: an active-card list, history table, filter bar, integrations card, system card, and backup/restore plan surfaces. TasksIndicator renders the animated badge in the sidebar rail showing in-progress count. All components consume TasksCtx from TasksProvider.
contexts.name: background-tasks-ui

contexts.description: Subscription billing via Polar: returns the entitlement overview (plan, per-meter allowances, prepaid credits), drives checkout session creation, redirects to the customer portal, and receives Polar webhook events that update the local entitlement state. Billing-routes test pins auth and response-shape contracts.
contexts.name: billing

contexts.description: Handles plan selection, checkout initiation, and the Stripe portal — the purchase-path half of the Billing tab. BillingPlanCatalog renders available plans and the minutes top-up pack; useBillingPortal opens the provider's self-service portal; billingPortalOpen and billingCheckoutBanner are pure state-machine helpers that control redirect and post-checkout banner behaviour. billingPlanPriceKind classifies price display (per-unit vs. flat) with unit tests.
contexts.name: billing-checkout-catalog

contexts.description: Integrates with Polar.sh as the subscription billing provider: webhook ingestion and signature verification, subscription sync, gateway abstraction, and price reconciliation between the local plan catalog and the Polar product objects. Keeps local billing state in sync with the upstream billing source of truth.
contexts.name: billing-integration

contexts.description: Defines the plan catalog (free, starter, growth, byom, enterprise) with per-meter limits for AI candidates, case designs, and interview minutes. Provides plan entitlement resolution, usage reduction logic, and enforcement guards that block feature access when the workspace has exhausted its allocation.
contexts.name: billing-plans

contexts.description: Renders the Billing settings tab — the recruiter-facing overview of their current plan, entitlement meters, and subscription status. Fetches GET /api/billing on mount, handles retry on load failure, and shows post-checkout confirmation via a derived banner state. Depends on billingCheckoutBanner state machine and the billing type contracts shared with the catalog.
contexts.name: billing-settings-ui

contexts.description: White-label branding editor (E3 enterprise feature) — lets an org admin set the workspace display name, primary accent color, and logo URL. The accent immediately re-skins the whole app (and candidate-facing pages) via an inline CSS variable override applied without a reload; a WCAG contrast guard blocks saving inaccessible accent colours. BrandingPreview renders a live side-panel preview as a lazily-loaded chunk.
contexts.name: brand-settings

contexts.description: White-label branding infrastructure for the workspace. `BrandProvider` seeds a React context with the tenant's display name, logo URL, and accent color; `BrandHeader` renders the brand mark in sidebar and header slots; `BrandStyle` injects a CSS variable for the brand accent color so all downstream token consumers pick it up automatically. Together they allow every tenant to present a personalized workspace identity without theme-level changes.
contexts.name: brand-theming

contexts.api_surface: Internal calibration helpers consumed by analysis scoring
contexts.description: Score calibration system that adjusts raw model scores against historical pipeline outcomes to reduce systematic bias. Holdout arm experiments (A/B test) compare calibrated vs uncalibrated decisions; the calibration model is periodically refitted from confirmed hiring outcomes.
contexts.name: calibration

contexts.description: EU AI Act Art. 72 calibration drift alarm: compares a frozen baseline calibration payload against a current window on three axes — Brier score degradation, PSI (population stability index) over the score distribution, and base-rate shift — and returns a structured verdict (stable/moderate_drift/significant_drift/insufficient_data). Pure deterministic; no LLM, no I/O. Honesty gate: never fires when either window is below the minOutcomes threshold.
contexts.name: calibration-drift-monitoring

contexts.description: Public-facing job application intake: handles standard, quick, and follow-up apply forms for a given job. Enforces knockout questions, deduplicates re-applicants, enriches the profile, dispatches the application-received comms, and creates the pipeline entry. Rate-limited and tested for acknowledgement and error hygiene contracts.
contexts.name: candidate-application

contexts.description: Handles the inbound candidate application flow: intake validation, CV upload constraints, profile extraction from uploaded CVs (autofill), variant scoring for multi-position matching, and the applicant profile resolver. This is the top-of-funnel that transforms a raw application into a scored pipeline entry.
contexts.name: candidate-apply

contexts.description: Job-candidate fit scoring: runs or reads the fit-score matrix for a JD against the analyzed candidate pool, surfaces match reasoning for individual scores, and provides salary benchmark lookups. The general benchmarks endpoint exposes market salary data used by the offer-draft and comp-confidence surfaces.
contexts.name: candidate-matching

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST /api/onboarding, GET/PUT /api/onboarding/[id], GET/POST /api/onboarding/candidate/[token], GET /api/invite/[token], GET /api/me/getting-started, GET/POST /api/me/onboarding
contexts.description: Post-hire onboarding hand-off: creates onboarding runs for Hired candidates from configurable templates and exposes a token-gated candidate-facing checklist. Also covers workspace-operator first-run: the getting-started checklist state and the me/onboarding setup wizard progress so new teams reach their first hire quickly.
contexts.name: candidate-onboarding

contexts.description: Manages the talent pool of previously-evaluated candidates and the rediscovery feature that resurfaces past applicants for new openings. Includes consent-gated reactivation, relevance ranking for re-engagement, and alert generation when a suitable past candidate is found for a role.
contexts.name: candidate-pool-rediscovery

contexts.description: Token-gated pre-boarding questionnaire presented to a new hire immediately after accepting an offer. The candidate visits a one-time URL containing their onboarding token, fills in logistical fields (preferred name, t-shirt size, dietary needs, equipment prefs, emergency contact, start-date confirmation), and submits answers that surface on the recruiter's hand-off tab. The client component fetches view state and posts answers to /api/onboarding/candidate/[token]; route-level loading and error boundaries provide resilient fallbacks.
contexts.name: candidate-preboarding-questionnaire

contexts.description: Archetype-aware candidate profile (v2): evidence-based skill model with provenance weights (observed > professional > personal_project > coursework), potential/readiness scoring for early-career candidates, and transformation into the MatchCandidate format the scoring engine consumes. Soft signals (overclaim, tenure instability, hidden strengths) are aggregated as a panel of hypotheses with confirmation probes, not verdicts.
contexts.name: candidate-profile-v2

contexts.description: Candidate CV profile management: CRUD for stored candidate profiles (the parsed CV records that feed the match engine), a draft creation flow that orchestrates text extraction + Python parsing before saving, and a bulk candidate-list read used by the profile management tab. Staleness and divergence signals let the UI flag profiles that should be re-analyzed.
contexts.name: candidate-profiles

contexts.description: Candidate-facing self-scheduling surface reached via a one-time tokenized link. The page loads available interview slots from `/api/schedule/[token]`, lets the candidate pick a time, and handles the full post-booking lifecycle: confirmation delivery status, RSVP (attend/cancel), reschedule (up to a server-gated cap), withdrawal, and a 'propose your own times' escalation when no offerable slots remain. Depends on the schedule API route, shared timezone/slot-label utilities, and the recruiter-side AddToCalendar component.
contexts.name: candidate-self-scheduling-page

contexts.description: Components that surface multi-dimensional candidate intelligence signals beyond the overall score. `Badge` is the single semantic badge component covering all pipeline qualitative signals — confidence levels, code-review status, interview recommendations (advance/hold/reject), fit tiers, and provenance indicators. `PotentialBadge` shows an explainable potential score for student and career-switcher candidates with a popover breakdown. `FactorChart` and `FactorChartBody` render a five-component breakdown bar chart. `GithubAnalysisPanel` displays GitHub profile analysis including language mix, top repos, skill matches, and a lightweight code-review signal.
contexts.name: candidate-signal-display

contexts.description: Orchestrates a full simulation round by running every `bundle-<persona>.json` file in a round folder through the production devcase evaluation pipeline (`pipeline.jobfit.devcase.devcase_cli evaluate-submission`) and writing the result to a matching `eval-<persona>.json`. After all personas are scored it prints a discrimination verdict — verifier must beat every canonical persona, delegator must rank last — and exits non-zero on failure, enabling CI-style assertion of pipeline health.
contexts.name: casesim-evaluator

contexts.description: Outbound communications table and management: shows all sent messages (offer letters, rejection notices, interview invites) in a table with per-row status; lets recruiters preview message content in a modal; and provides a resend flow for bounced emails. The comms helpers derive display state from raw message records.
contexts.name: channels-comms

contexts.description: The Channels tab shell — the "Intake Studio" — with an icon-pill section switcher (one tab per intake channel type, each carrying its own accent color and live-status badge) and the stage frame that leads every section with a hero band, stat cluster, and manager component. Accent and section metadata are static config consumed by the switcher.
contexts.name: channels-core-ui

contexts.description: Data-access hooks for the Channels tab: useChannelsData fetches webhooks, published jobs, and accepted-count in parallel and exposes a reload trigger; useChannelsReceivers fetches the receiver list with a liveness predicate (isReceiverLive checks whether an authenticated POST has arrived). Consumed by both the intake and comms surfaces.
contexts.name: channels-data

contexts.description: Inbound CV intake management: email-forwarding wizard (guided setup for role-specific inboxes), receiver table (one row per configured webhook receiver), add-receiver modal, Gmail/Outlook setup guide with copy-chip, CV simulation card for testing the intake path, relay config card, job ad form pane for careers-page posting, and filter/filter-menu for narrowing the receiver list.
contexts.name: channels-intake

contexts.description: i18n honesty test that verifies all string keys used on the Channels tab resolve through the translation catalog in every supported locale, catching hardcoded English strings or orphaned keys.
contexts.name: channels-tests

contexts.description: The core outbound communications engine: envelope assembly (to/from/subject/body), recipient resolution, relay configuration (env-first, then stored config), delivery truth flag, status tracking (sent/bounced/failed), and the tenancy guard that prevents cross-workspace comm reads. Every recruitmen event (rejection, offer, outreach) routes through this layer.
contexts.name: comms-dispatch

contexts.description: Renders the recruiter-facing view of sent/received communications and handles locale-aware message templating. comms-view formats the display record from the raw delivery log; comms-locale resolves the language for outbound messages based on candidate locale; lead-intake and lead-payload handle the inbound sourcing lead flow.
contexts.name: comms-view-locale

contexts.api_surface: GET /api/comms, POST /api/comms/[id]/resend, POST /api/comms/callback, GET /api/comms/capability, GET/PUT /api/comms/relay, POST /api/comms/relay/test, GET/POST /api/channels/webhooks, POST /api/channels/inbound/[token], POST /api/channels/webhooks/[token]
contexts.description: Recruiter outbox and relay management: reads the derived comms view (sent, failed, bounced, recovered states), resends dead-letters, and manages the email relay configuration. The callback endpoint receives async bounce/delivery receipts from the relay provider, and the inbound channel receiver handles webhook-sourced applications from job boards. Channel webhook management lets recruiters bind job+language pairs to public inbound URLs.
contexts.name: communications

contexts.description: Pure stateless reducer implementing the two-step arm/confirm safety gate for consequential control-room actions — approving human gates, applying a suggested promote floor, and triggering reconcile. A first click arms the control without executing; a second click on the same control executes and disarms, preventing accidental irreversible actions from a misclick on a live-polling UI. Accompanied by unit tests (node:test, no DOM) that pin the non-vacuous contract.
contexts.name: control-room-action-guard

contexts.description: Public chat-based application flow where candidates answer knockout questions and identity steps in a step-by-step conversation before being placed into the pipeline as Accepted or Declined. The server page builds the localized script and resolves lead-enrichment prefill (?lead= token) server-side, then hands it to the ConversationalApply client component which runs the step machine, persists an in-progress draft to localStorage (fingerprinted against the script so a job edit or locale switch discards the stale draft), and POSTs collected answers to /api/apply/[id]. Depends on apply-intake, completeness-followup, and cv-autofill libs, and cross-references the quick-apply flow for the enrichment hand-off.
contexts.name: conversational-apply-flow

contexts.description: Custom SVG icon components for the five CV analysis result tab labels — Extraction, Job Fit, Salary, Interview, and Compare — that have no suitable Lucide equivalents. Each is a self-contained, fill-inheriting SVG so it naturally takes the parent text color in both themes. Exported via a barrel index for clean imports.
contexts.name: custom-icons

contexts.description: Headless terminal scripts that invoke the same pipeline analysis service the UI uses, rendering focused slices (overview, comparison, job-fit, salary, interview questions) to stdout without a browser. They share a common ANSI rendering helper (_common.py) and accept a CV file plus an optional job description via CLI flags. Entry point for rapid, scriptable CV analysis outside the web app.
contexts.name: cv-analysis-cli

contexts.description: Orchestrates the full CV analysis pipeline: text extraction, PII checks, authenticity signals, Gemini analysis, salary estimation, company context, keyword coverage, and interview kit generation into a single AnalysisResult. The service.py entry point is called by Next.js API routes; pipeline.py owns the multi-stage logic with per-stage timing logs. Summary formatting for seed scripts is co-located.
contexts.name: cv-analysis-orchestration

contexts.description: The master CV analysis result display system. `ResultPanel` orchestrates a tabbed panel (up to 6 tabs) and above the tabs renders a `VerdictBanner` (colored score+band lead), `ArchetypeBanner` (candidate archetype with Save-as-profile action), and `QualityStrip` (sanity check results). `DispositionEditor` lets a recruiter record their screening decision inline; `AddToPipelineButton` acts on a job-fit read immediately. `verdict.ts` computes the authoritative overall score and winner label for multi-variant runs. The extraction tab shows raw CV data; the compare tab shows a side-by-side multi-variant score delta table.
contexts.name: cv-analysis-results-panel

contexts.description: Quality gate harness for the CV analysis pipeline: runner.py drives batch evaluation over fixture profiles, thresholds.py holds pass/fail score floors, and seed_cv_fixtures.py generates synthetic CVs via Gemini for the CSAS pilot corpus. Provides both a CLI entry point and a threshold-based CI gate, with styled output for terminal readability.
contexts.name: cv-eval-harness

contexts.description: Extracts and normalizes candidate CV text from PDF, DOCX, and other formats, then submits it to Gemini for multimodal structured analysis. The extraction layer handles encoding repair (Czech mojibake), resource bounds, and defusedxml safety. Gemini returns a structured profile JSON including skills, seniority, salary, and role family, while the embedding bridge provides vector representations for similarity search.
contexts.name: cv-text-extraction

contexts.description: Three deterministic trust layers applied before and after LLM analysis: authenticity heuristics detect AI-generated or embellished CVs via buzzword density and implausible claims; credential checks gate regulated roles (FINRA, nursing, bar admission) against expired or missing licences; PII redaction masks identity signals for blind-screening mode. All are pure and unit-testable, emitting sanity-check sentences into the trust ledger.
contexts.name: cv-trust-signals

contexts.description: Implements the right-to-erasure (GDPR Art. 17): full candidate data scrub across analyses and pipeline, secret redaction to prevent PII leaking into logs, and the reinstate-seal test that verifies sealed decision records cannot be retroactively altered after erasure.
contexts.name: data-erasure

contexts.api_surface: Internal repository consumed by analytics and billing API routes
contexts.description: Repository layer for analytics aggregates, LLM usage tracking, salary benchmarks, and org-level performance benchmarks. The LLM usage table meters AI consumption for billing; analytics tables power the hiring-funnel dashboard; benchmark tables hold market comparison data.
contexts.name: db-analytics-llm

contexts.api_surface: Internal repository consumed by /api/comms and /api/campaign routes
contexts.description: Repository layer for the communications hub: the channels table (email/Slack/webhook per workspace) and campaign_packs (AI-generated job-posting copy). Provides workspace-scoped CRUD so the comms dispatch layer knows which channels are configured for each team.
contexts.name: db-comms-channels

contexts.api_surface: Internal DB connection exported to all db/* modules
contexts.description: The SQLite connection singleton and migration runner (better-sqlite3), plus workspace and user repository primitives. Provides the canonical DB file path resolution, a portability layer for expressions that differ between SQLite and PostgreSQL, and the boot-time tenancy assertion.
contexts.name: db-core

contexts.api_surface: Internal repository consumed by interview and devcase routes
contexts.description: Repository layer for interview records, developer case submissions, and tokenized skill profiles. Handles multi-tenant CRUD for interview session data, devcase lifecycle rows, and the rotating-token skill-profile store used by AI scoring.
contexts.name: db-interviews-devcase

contexts.api_surface: Internal repository consumed by org/team API routes
contexts.description: Repository layer for organizations, team memberships, and workspace invitations. These tables back the multi-tenant identity model: an organization can have many workspaces (teams), each workspace has members with roles, and invites are the entry point for adding users.
contexts.name: db-org-members

contexts.api_surface: Internal repository functions consumed by API routes
contexts.description: Repository layer for the core recruitment data: pipeline entries, candidate profiles, job records, analysis results, and background tasks. These are the central tables driving the recruiter dashboard — every candidate card, stage move, and analysis report reads from here.
contexts.name: db-pipeline-profiles

contexts.description: Portable dump-and-restore pair for the SQLite workspace (data/kp.sqlite). db-dump.mjs serialises every table's DDL and rows into a single JSON file; db-load.mjs restores that file onto any machine, with conservative semantics (no-overwrite by default, full transaction, schema-first so app boot migrations can carry an older dump forward). Used for seeding fresh checkouts, sharing demo state, and cross-machine dev setup.
contexts.name: db-snapshot-restore

contexts.description: Immutable audit log for every automated and human hiring decision. Each sealed decision record captures the rule version, score snapshot, fairness hash, and approval attribution at the moment the decision was made — enabling EU AI Act compliance evidence and post-hoc audit. The config schema governs screening thresholds that feed into the automation engine.
contexts.name: decision-records

contexts.description: Renders individual AI review cards that surface the model's recommendation for each candidate, with accept/reject actions, score staleness indicators, and a summary modal that shows the full analysis body. Also handles bulk-select mode so recruiters can batch-decide a set of AI-reviewed candidates at once.
contexts.name: decisions-ai-review

contexts.description: EU AI Act compliance section within the decisions flow: computes a candidate's compliance impact tier, shows a structured impact-check panel, and renders the compliance section block in the decisions UI. Ensures that AI-assisted hiring decisions meet regulatory disclosure requirements.
contexts.name: decisions-compliance

contexts.description: Pure business logic for group evaluation: skill-row construction, salary scale computation, lead-story ranking, localization of evaluation output, session-cache keying, and the useGroupEval hook that derives all modal state from a cached evaluation payload. DOM-free and unit-pinnable.
contexts.name: decisions-group-eval-logic

contexts.description: The group-evaluation modal that lets recruiters compare a shortlisted cohort side-by-side: a comparison table with per-skill rows, an AI verdict panel, salary cells with benchmark context, fairness guard panel, per-candidate tab view, risk indicators, and both enriched and legacy layout paths. Consumes the evaluation payload from the LLM call and presents structured accept/reject affordances.
contexts.name: decisions-group-eval-ui

contexts.description: The Decisions tab shell: AI-review queue, key-decisions role rows, reconsider queue, modal wiring, and all associated state in useDecisionsQueue. Recruiters act on AI-surfaced shortlists here, send screening waves, and reinstate previously rejected candidates from the reconsider queue.
contexts.name: decisions-queue-core

contexts.description: Business rules enforcement for the decisions queue: floor-disclosure logic that warns when an accepted candidate is below a configured salary floor, selection-hygiene pruning that removes stale entry IDs from a saved group-eval selection, and the rules-configuration modal for recruiters. These are pure utilities with no UI dependencies beyond the modal.
contexts.name: decisions-rules-hygiene

contexts.description: The screening-wave feature that lets a recruiter bulk-send rejection notices to all candidates in a rejection cohort in one click. The modal lists the affected candidates grouped by reason, a confirm step guards against accidental sends, and the wave hook handles the API call and result reporting.
contexts.name: decisions-screen-wave

contexts.description: Unit tests for decisions business logic: score-staleness computation, floor-disclosure edge cases, selection-hygiene pruning, group-eval robustness (pool drift, empty cohorts), offer-card score edge cases, fairness-guard correctness, comparison lead-crown ranking, lead-story output, and group-eval localization.
contexts.name: decisions-tests

contexts.api_surface: POST /api/sim/inbound, POST /api/sim/apply-cv, POST /api/sim/screen-draft, POST /api/sim/offer-draft, GET /api/sim/offer-link, POST /api/sim/reset
contexts.description: Guided product demo simulation engine: injects synthetic candidates into the pipeline (inbound application, CV-attached apply), generates simulated screening-draft decisions, creates offer-draft links, and provides a reset endpoint that purges all SIM-marked rows. Scope tests verify that sim writes target the demo workspace and never corrupt the operator's real pipeline.
contexts.name: demo-simulation

contexts.description: A dev-only click-to-copy source-path overlay that lets developers right-click any rendered element to copy its `File.tsx:LINE` reference directly to the clipboard for use in Claude Code or other editors. It is activated by launching with `npm run dev:inspect` (which stamps host elements with `data-loc` attributes via a Babel pass) and toggled via keyboard shortcuts (`;` → `i` to arm, `Esc` to exit). The tool is gated behind `process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development'` in the root layout and ships zero bytes to production.
contexts.name: dev-inspector

contexts.description: Dev-only click-to-source tooling for the in-app DevInspector overlay (press `;` then `i`). A Babel plugin (inject-source-loc.cjs) stamps host JSX elements with data-loc attributes at compile time; a webpack/Turbopack pre-loader (source-loc-loader.cjs) wires that plugin into the build when DEV_INSPECT=1. Enables mapping any clicked DOM node back to its source file and line, working around React 19's removal of _debugSource.
contexts.name: dev-inspector-tooling

contexts.description: Scripts that control the local development environment. dev-guard.mjs wraps any long-running dev command and ensures the full process tree (including Windows orphan workers) is killed on exit, with an optional circuit breaker for node-process storms. dev-empty.mjs launches a brand-new empty-tenant instance on port 3002 against a throwaway SQLite file, reaping any stale prior instance first, so the first-run onboarding experience can be verified without touching real data.
contexts.name: dev-server-management

contexts.description: Candidate-facing dev case assignment page reached via a recruiter-minted bearer token. Resolves the posting and dev case from SQLite, renders the probe-safe Markdown brief, and routes the candidate to either a live-work workspace or a repo-link submission form depending on whether a seed bundle was materialized at posting creation. Handles closed postings with an honest closure card and exposes an AI-use disclosure.
contexts.name: devcase-candidate-apply

contexts.description: Implements pipeline phases D5/D8 (reflect.py) and D6 (evaluate.py): reflect.py infers where a candidate mentally went from durable repository signals (commit sizes, cadence, file tree, messages) using LLM interpretation of structural shape rather than keyword checklists; evaluate.py fuses the commit reflection and tooling signal against the case rubric to score the five durable capabilities (problem framing, tooling fluency, judgment/verification, architecture, transfer), then scores capability transfer to the specific role. Both uphold the fairness invariant that AI use is never a penalty.
contexts.name: devcase-candidate-evaluation

contexts.description: Implements pipeline phases D2 (analyze.py) and D3 (design.py): first reflects a hiring need against the real body of work the role acts on (codebase for software, own materials for other functions) to surface stated-vs-real gaps, then turns the need + reality analysis into a RoleSpec and a CaseScenario baking in covert tooling probes (ambiguity, legacy traps, mid-flight requirement changes) that assess judgment rather than output volume. Both steps use an LLM path (Claude CLI) with a deterministic fallback and self-rated confidence propagation.
contexts.name: devcase-case-generation

contexts.description: Implements the two in-session chat personas available inside the Live Work Surface: the candidate's own work assistant (sees only candidate-visible material; grades how they drive the model, not what it produces) and the hiring-team stakeholder (sees internal probe decision spaces to stay consistent with designed ambiguity but must never resolve ambiguities or confirm traps). Both channels are routed through the platform so the dialogue becomes observed evidence graded by prompt_signals.py. Uses the shared provenance runner for LLM path plus a deterministic 'unavailable' fallback.
contexts.name: devcase-chat-channels

contexts.description: devcase_cli.py is the unified CLI entry point mirroring automation_cli/reasoning_cli — it routes all pipeline commands (analyze-need, design-artifacts, reflect-commits, evaluate-submission, interview-scenario, materialize-seed, session-chat, baseline-solve) and wraps every output in a uniform provenance envelope (source tri-state, perStepSources, fallbackReason, confidence) so the UI has a single stable contract; provenance.py owns the provenance envelope logic and the shared LLM-or-deterministic fallback runner used by every generation step; source.py provides deterministic candidate sourcing by normalizing a RoleSpec into a Job and ranking the existing candidate DB against it using the core matching engine.
contexts.name: devcase-cli-integration

contexts.description: Core developer case (technical assessment) infrastructure: seed generation, orchestrator that drives the case lifecycle (need analysis → scenario → solve → evaluate → promote), dev control policy (autonomy level, promote floor), and simulation store for the guided pipeline demo mode.
contexts.name: devcase-core

contexts.api_surface: CLI: python -m pipeline.jobfit.devcase.calibrate, python -m pipeline.jobfit.devcase.real_corpus; External: Hugging Face datasets-server REST API
contexts.description: Stress-tests the case-generation pipeline against real, broad, cross-industry office job descriptions instead of synthetic ones: real_corpus.py pulls real JDs from the Hugging Face datasets-server REST API, classifies them by role-family and seniority, stratifies a reproducible ~100-JD sample forcing breadth across families, and converts each into a devcase Scenario; calibrate.py drives the full production design chain over that corpus and reports health signals plus optionally runs the LLM judge with independence tracking. This harness exists specifically to harden the generator against the known bank/Czech/tech industry-lock.
contexts.name: devcase-corpus-calibration

contexts.description: Inner panels rendered inside the DevCaseDetail shell for specific views — Internal notes/team discussion, Shortlist of top-ranked candidates, Channels (where the case is distributed), and the InterviewKit for shortlisted candidates. Also hosts the OutboxSection that shows comms outbox items tied to a case. These panels are lazy-loaded after the user navigates to a specific case.
contexts.name: devcase-detail-panels

contexts.description: Defines the Pydantic data models that flow through the entire dev-case lifecycle: DevNeed → NeedAnalysis → (CaseScenario + RoleSpec) → Submission → (CommitReflection + ToolingSignal) → CaseEvaluation → TransferAssessment. Uses camelCase aliasing so artifacts round-trip cleanly to the TypeScript front-end. Also contains the RUBRIC_DIMENSIONS constant that defines the five durable capability axes graded throughout evaluation.
contexts.name: devcase-domain-models

contexts.description: The quality-gating harness for both halves of the pipeline: lifecycle_eval.py runs the design-half (need → analysis → role+case) over a synthetic scenario landscape in parallel and reports reliability and quality signals without an LLM; lifecycle_audits.py adds LLM-as-judge quality scoring and binary role-fit audits; submission_eval.py runs the evaluation-half over synthetic candidate behaviors and enforces four gated properties (reliability, fairness, discrimination, quality); llm_judge.py is the shared judge plumbing that routes grading through a separate 'devcase_judge' provider seat so the judge is never the same model that produced the artifacts it grades.
contexts.name: devcase-eval-harness

contexts.api_surface: Internal evaluation pipeline consumed by devcase-orchestrator
contexts.description: Evaluates developer case submissions: authenticity checks (anti-delegation controls including prompt capture, canaries, watermark, perturbation, and baseline diff), cohort ranking, comparative scoring, feedback generation, and the interview-kit extractor that derives follow-up interview questions from the submitted solution. Dev outcomes tracks historical assessment results.
contexts.name: devcase-evaluation

contexts.api_surface: GET /api/devcase/lifecycle, POST /api/devcase/lifecycle/[id]/approve, POST /api/devcase/lifecycle/[id]/close, POST /api/devcase/lifecycle/[id]/redesign, GET/POST /api/devcase/session, GET /api/devcase/session/[id], POST /api/devcase/session/[id]/chat, POST /api/devcase/session/[id]/submit
contexts.description: Dev case session lifecycle: candidate session creation, real-time chat turns, final submission, and recruiter lifecycle transitions (approve, close, redesign). The approve gate enforces probe-strength doctrine via a shared guard; close carries tenancy isolation tests to prevent cross-workspace leaks.
contexts.name: devcase-lifecycle

contexts.description: Manages the full lifecycle of a developer case from creation through close — the main DevTab entry point, the cases-list view, lifecycle section rows and review panel, case publishing (token generation, channel creation), and seed materialization. useDevTabData loads all server state (cases, postings, lifecycles, outbox); useDevTabActions dispatches transitions. DevCaseDetail.publish.ts and .seed.ts handle the approve → publish → seed flow.
contexts.name: devcase-lifecycle-management

contexts.description: In-browser live coding workspace that presents the materialized seed files to the candidate, records process-telemetry events (edits, evals), and persists a local draft so sessions survive a page reload. The draft is encoded/decoded with strict size and shape bounds before being flushed to the server via the same inbound webhook as the repo-link form. Includes a unit-test suite covering round-trip fidelity, garbage inputs, and size-cap enforcement.
contexts.name: devcase-live-work-surface

contexts.description: Implements the six LLM-era anti-delegation integrity controls: artifact_checks.py provides deterministic canary-outcome grading (were planted flaws addressed/flagged/propagated?) and baseline similarity scoring (how much did the human add beyond a one-shot model solve?); baseline.py freezes that naive one-shot baseline at case approval; prompt_signals.py derives fairness-conscious signals from the captured assistant/stakeholder chat transcript (decomposition, iteration, verification asks, brief-paste ratio); process_events.py derives tooling signals from an observed server-recorded process event stream (opens, edits, decision-log writes, perturbation reveal moment). All four are purely deterministic and unit-testable without an LLM.
contexts.name: devcase-llm-era-controls

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST /api/devcase, POST /api/devcase/publish, POST /api/devcase/promote, POST /api/devcase/inbound, POST /api/devcase/submit, GET /api/devcase/outcomes, GET/POST /api/devcase/comms, GET /api/devcase/source, GET /api/devcase/skill-profile
contexts.description: Developer case scenario authoring and delivery: the recruiter-facing CRUD for case scenarios (approve, publish, promote), the candidate-facing inbound submission handler, and the outbound comms/posting dispatch. Includes the skill-profile generator and the source/feedback read paths that close the authoring loop.
contexts.name: devcase-management

contexts.description: The first stage of the developer assessment workflow — capturing the hiring need (role, seniority, repo URLs) via DevNeedForm, then running AI analysis to produce a case design (role spec + scenario + rubric) surfaced in DevAnalysisView, DevAnalysisDesignCard, and DevAnalysisReflectionCard. The define-view tab and switcher orchestrate which design step is active. Depends on the JD library for pre-filled role context.
contexts.name: devcase-need-and-design

contexts.description: Provides the full landscape of synthetic test material used by both the design and evaluation harnesses: scenarios.py generates domain-pluggable hiring scenarios (IT, marketing, finance, sales, design) with planted defects for health-eval; submission_scenarios.py generates synthetic candidate work traces across verifies/usesAI/strong/weak axes for the fairness and discrimination gates; _synth.py holds the shared deterministic round-robin helpers so both generators stay in sync; interview_scenario.py generates the canonical six-phase AI-interview scenario per case; seed_materializer.py materializes repo prose into a concrete starter file tree carrying the case's planted traps.
contexts.name: devcase-scenario-library

contexts.description: Shared types, helpers, and display primitives used across the entire devcase feature — DevTypes defines all domain types (need, design, submission, evaluation, lifecycle, posting), DevHelpers provides formatting and source-descriptor utilities, DevShared has layout primitives (DevSection), DevScoreBar renders the score visualization, DevProvenanceStrip shows LLM provenance, and DevApplyTokenPill renders the apply link token. Used by all other devcase contexts.
contexts.name: devcase-shared-primitives

contexts.description: Handles collecting candidate submissions against a dev case and running AI evaluation — the submission form for attaching a repo/notes, the submission row with outcome pill and skill-profile chip, and the full evaluation panel (scores by rubric dimension, process trace, compare view, cohort probe, authenticity band). devEvalTaskState tracks background evaluation task state. Evaluation results feed the shortlist and transfer-score ranking.
contexts.name: devcase-submission-evaluation

contexts.description: Stop hook that enforces documentation currency after every assistant turn. It walks the turn's JSONL transcript for file edits, matches changed paths against the feature-doc coupling map (feature-doc-map.json), and exits non-zero naming the doc that must be updated when mapped feature source changes without a corresponding docs/ edit. The test suite (check-doc-sync.test.mjs) validates the hook logic and verifies every mapped doc exists and every glob root resolves.
contexts.name: doc-sync-hook

contexts.description: End-to-end smoke tests for the consolidated CV Analyze flow, covering CV-only, CV+JD, CV+JD+company, and full CV+JD+company+GitHub pipeline paths. Tests exercise the LLM-backed analysis route against a running app, validate rendered result panels (Score Breakdown, Salary, Job fit, GitHub tabs), and include a WCAG accessibility gate using axe-core. GitHub API calls are stubbed by default via a Playwright route interceptor to eliminate rate-limit flake.
contexts.name: e2e-cv-analysis-smoke

contexts.description: Thin test helper that seeds the workspace-entry cookie (`kp_entered`) needed to bypass the HomeGate server guard before each E2E test. Encapsulates the cookie name and URL so that if the session contract changes, only this file needs updating. Used as a beforeEach hook across all e2e spec files that navigate to protected workspace routes.
contexts.name: e2e-dev-auth

contexts.description: Deterministic E2E tests for the shared Modal component's keyboard-dismiss contract, specifically guarding the bug where Escape failed to close the dialog when focus had drifted to `<body>` (a node-bound listener never fired in that state). Drives the Decision-rules modal, which is always available without LLM keys or seeded data. Covers Escape from body focus, Escape from auto-focused control, and backdrop click dismissal.
contexts.name: e2e-modal-escape

contexts.description: Deterministic end-to-end tests for the candidate profile builder flow, covering archetype routing (Experienced→bau and Student→student) and completeness scoring without any LLM dependency. Tests drive the guided intake form, validate the in-DOM preview panel (archetype pill, completeness progress bar, nudge text), and verify the full save round-trip by asserting the POST response and a subsequent GET against /api/profile.
contexts.name: e2e-profile-builder

contexts.description: Typed Playwright fixture providing a deterministic GitHub analysis payload and a route-stub helper for the `/api/github-analysis` endpoint. The fixture is typed against the production `GithubAnalysis` schema so shape drift between the route, schema, and fixture surfaces as a compile error rather than a silent test mismatch. Eliminates the 60 req/hr anonymous GitHub API rate-limit that previously caused flaky failures.
contexts.name: e2e-test-fixtures

contexts.description: Data export utilities for generating downloadable reports: candidate lists, pipeline exports, and analysis result CSVs. Provides the serialization helpers and file naming conventions used by export endpoints.
contexts.name: export-data

contexts.description: Provides the complete set of styled form input controls used across every recruiter-facing workspace surface. Includes single-line text, multi-line text, checkbox, radio, file upload, rich text editor, segmented toggle, and accessible select. All inputs share a consistent Tailwind token baseline so they reflow identically across Studio Light and Spark Dark themes.
contexts.name: form-primitives

contexts.description: GDPR consent tracking and data-held registry: candidate consent records with TTL display, the set of personal data fields held per candidate, and the compliance-regime resolver that maps jurisdiction to applicable rules. This is the legal basis layer for storing and processing candidate data.
contexts.name: gdpr-consent

contexts.description: Public, token-gated GDPR self-service page that lets candidates view what personal data the platform holds and request erasure (right to erasure / Art. 17 GDPR). The candidate receives a tokenised link in email footers; the page fetches their data summary from /api/data/[token] and posts an erasure request to the same endpoint, scrubbing PII while retaining the de-identified recruitment record. Rendered as a client component so the token param drives per-request fetching without blocking the prerendered shell.
contexts.name: gdpr-data-erasure-page

contexts.api_surface: GitHub REST API (outbound), consumed by analysis pipeline
contexts.description: Fetches and summarises a candidate's public GitHub presence: repo snapshot (top repos, commit activity), code-quality evidence extraction, safe URL validation for profile links, and the GitHub handle resolver for pipeline entries. Feeds into the AI analysis as a supplementary signal alongside the CV.
contexts.name: github-analysis

contexts.description: Shared types and URL grammar for the group-evaluation (head-to-head comparison) feature. groupEvalTypes.ts defines Fairness, FairnessScheme, RobustnessStatus, Comparison, and isFairnessAligned — the validated fairness-blob guard that degrades a malformed payload to an honest 'could not assess' panel instead of crashing. groupEvalArm.ts owns the pure, dependency-free `?arm=` deep-link grammar (buildArmParam / parseArmParam / seedArmSelection) that lets the Match tab pre-arm a Decisions group-eval selection without auto-firing a paid LLM run.
contexts.name: group-eval-shared

contexts.description: Comparative evaluation of a shortlisted cohort for a single role: generates a structured group assessment highlighting differentiators, enforces governance rules (diversity guards, selection cache to prevent re-running expensive evaluations), and persists results in the group_evals store. Powers the Decisions tab's side-by-side comparison view.
contexts.name: group-evaluation

contexts.description: Computes hiring funnel analytics: stage-by-stage conversion bottlenecks, forecast of time-to-hire, pipeline momentum (velocity trends), offer acceptance rates, source channel attribution, and split-test ad performance comparison. Feeds the analytics dashboard with actionable hiring metrics.
contexts.name: hiring-analytics

contexts.api_surface: GET/PUT /api/decisions/config, POST /api/decisions/screen-wave, GET /api/decisions/group-eval, POST /api/decisions/reconsider, GET /api/decisions/records, GET/POST/PUT /api/archetypes, GET/PUT /api/archetypes/[id]
contexts.description: Structured screening decisions: the decision config (score thresholds, auto-reject rules), the screen-wave batch auto-rejector, group evaluation (LLM-powered cross-candidate comparison for a role), reconsideration of sealed decisions, and the immutable decision records audit trail. Archetypes (candidate personas used for fit classification) are managed here as they directly feed the decision engine.
contexts.name: hiring-decisions

contexts.description: CI gate that enforces parity between the default (en) locale catalog and every other locale. It checks for missing keys, orphan keys, and ICU placeholder mismatches using the same intl-messageformat parser next-intl uses at runtime. Exits non-zero on any violation, acting as the cross-locale complement to the compile-time TS Messages type augmentation.
contexts.name: i18n-integrity-check

contexts.api_surface: setLocale server action (writes NEXT_LOCALE cookie); getServerLocale() shared by rendering and API routes
contexts.description: Defines the supported locale universe (en, cs, de, fr) and the single resolution path used everywhere in the app: cookie → Accept-Language header → default. Provides the Locale type, isLocale guard, and resolveAcceptLanguage helper so locale switching is type-safe and can never write an unsupported value. Consumed by next-intl's request config for rendering and by server-side API routes that need to thread the active locale into backend pipeline calls.
contexts.name: i18n-locale-resolution

contexts.api_surface: Server-side runtime helpers, no direct API surface
contexts.description: Runtime infrastructure utilities: environment variable loader and validation, structured logger, rate limiter for API route protection, retry-sync for transient failures, Python subprocess runner (used by the automation pass), theme resolution, timezone utilities, OG image font loader, and the offline/load-state helpers for client resilience.
contexts.name: infra-runtime

contexts.description: Evaluation harness for the AI interviewer quality: interview_eval.py runs structured interview scenarios against golden answers, interview_optimize.py tunes prompts, and interview_scenarios_gen.py generates new scenario/golden-answer pairs. automation_eval.py measures end-to-end automation task quality. Language lock fixtures ensure locale correctness across the eval pipeline.
contexts.name: interview-eval-harness

contexts.description: Generates mock interview kits grounded in the candidate's specific CV gaps against a target role: 8-12 questions split into behavioral, technical, and red-flag-defense buckets, each tied to an evidence gap and decorated with a STAR-style answer scaffold. The rubrics JSON defines scoring dimensions and the interview-script JSON holds structured question templates.
contexts.name: interview-kit-generation

contexts.description: Internal A/B testing harness for evaluating realtime voice interview providers (OpenAI Realtime vs ElevenLabs). The page is gated behind the INTERVIEW_LAB_ENABLED env flag and bypasses the production tokenized session path, allowing engineers to compare speech quality, latency, turn-taking, and transcript fidelity across providers without a candidate token. It mounts VoiceInterviewClient which handles provider selection, audio connection, and live transcript capture.
contexts.name: interview-lab-harness

contexts.description: Locale and i18n support for interview and lead flows: language detection, locale resolution, and locale-aware message formatting shared across the interview and lead-intake paths.
contexts.name: interview-lead-locale

contexts.description: Orchestrates the structured interview lifecycle beyond the voice call itself: AI-generated interview prep kits, rubric generation, live interview run recording, structured scorecard evaluation, transcript storage, and recommendation synthesis. Also handles student-mode persona rules and post-interview reminder scheduling.
contexts.name: interview-orchestration

contexts.description: Candidate-facing tokenized portal that runs a first-round AI voice screening. Validates the session token against the SQLite store, enforces expiry/revocation, renders the run-of-show agenda via InterviewSidebar, and mounts VoiceInterviewClient for the live call. On completion it redirects the candidate to their durable /status link.
contexts.name: interview-portal

contexts.description: Structured interview preparation: per-candidate scorecard generation and import (merging results from an external scorecard store), plus a public token-gated skill-profile verification endpoint that candidates use to prove competencies before the interview. Feeds the pre-interview checklist and the post-interview comparison view.
contexts.name: interview-prep

contexts.description: The interview preparation result tab showing the AI-generated question kit tailored to the specific candidate and role. Questions are categorized into behavioral, technical, and red-flag-defense buckets with STAR scaffolds and the CV evidence gap that prompted each question. A filter bar lets recruiters focus by bucket. If the candidate is already on the pipeline board, a one-click button imports the questions into their live interview-prep artifact. Also surfaces soft signals (cultural and communication red flags) from CV text.
contexts.name: interview-prep-results

contexts.description: Self-scheduling invite lifecycle: recruiters create and bulk-send schedule invites with proposed time slots; candidates confirm, decline, or reschedule via a token URL. The route also handles no-show marking, meeting-URL injection, and reconcile flags that surface scheduling gaps in the recruiter's Schedule tab.
contexts.name: interview-scheduling

contexts.description: The interview simulation entry panel within the tools area — lets a recruiter (or student) pick a simulation mode (quick screen vs case-based), view what constructs will be assessed, and launch a voice interview session. InterviewAttachToCandidate links a running or completed session to a specific candidate record. Delegates to the voice interview infrastructure for the actual session.
contexts.name: interview-sim-launcher

contexts.description: AI-driven text-plane interview simulation for testing and calibration: runs a synthetic candidate persona through the voice interview flow without a real audio connection. The attach sub-route binds a simulation session to an existing interview session token so the test harness can drive it programmatically.
contexts.name: interview-simulation

contexts.description: Public token-gated page that lets a newly invited user accept their organisation invite, set a display name (if needed), and choose a password. The server shell resolves the token from the URL and hands it to a client form component that fetches a preview from GET /api/invite/[token] then POSTs credentials on submit. Depends on the member-roles lib and auth UI primitives (TextInput, recipes).
contexts.name: invite-accept-flow

contexts.api_surface: POST /api/analyze, GET /api/analyses, GET /api/analyses/[slug], GET /api/jds/[slug]/analyses, POST /api/jds/[slug]/retry-analysis, POST /api/extract-text, GET/POST /api/github-analysis
contexts.description: CV and JD AI analysis pipeline: runs Gemini/Claude to score a candidate CV against a JD, retries failed analyses, and stores results that feed fit scores and the pipeline board. Also handles GitHub profile deep-analysis (repo evidence, commit signal) and raw CV text extraction as a pre-step.
contexts.name: jd-analysis

contexts.description: Implements the backgrounded JD authoring workflow: a multi-field form (title, company, seniority, role family, prose need, repo URL, output language) that submits to the Generate pipeline and tracks the async build task while the recruiter navigates away. It also hosts the inline modal editor for opening a saved JD's body for edits, including a staged-suggestion banner when a coach handoff pre-fills a change. The context owns form state, template prefill resolution, live advisory lint (builderLintFindings), the save-as-draft path, and the generate-panel progress display.
contexts.name: jd-builder

contexts.description: Provides the recruiter-facing filterable table of all saved Job Descriptions, with per-row status chips, ingest affordances, detail panels, and a coach-trace note when a winnability handoff can't stage into the editor. The ledger fetches all JD rows from /api/jds, derives filter/sort/facet state from jdsLibrary pure helpers, and renders a scrollable table whose rows expand into a detail rail or modal. It depends on jdsLedgerLogic for state, jdsLedgerArtifacts for artifact-shape access, and jdsLedgerNav for deep-link open/close routing.
contexts.name: jd-ledger

Templates are fetched at builder mount to seed the template picker dropdown.
contexts.name: jd-template-manager

contexts.description: Pre-publish JD advisor that tells a recruiter whether a draft job description will actually fill. Runs counterfactual re-runs against the live candidate pool using production scorers: eligible/qualified counts, loosen-a-gate deltas (which language requirement blocks the most candidates), demote-a-must-have deltas, and salary vs market comparison. Pure deterministic logic — no LLM, no I/O.
contexts.name: jd-winnability-coach

contexts.api_surface: ko_filter(), score_job(), generate_reasoning(); CLI: match_cli.py, matrix_cli.py
contexts.description: Three-layer matching engine: KO filter (hard gates on seniority, education, language, work-mode), multi-factor scorer (skills with provenance weights, career fit, personal fit → weighted total with confidence band), and optional LLM reasoning layer. Archetype-aware weighting means early-career candidates are scored on potential rather than tenure. CLI bridges expose the engine to Next.js API routes.
contexts.name: job-candidate-matching

contexts.description: The job-fit result tab that shows how well a candidate matches the specific job description. Displays a standalone job-fit score (separate from the overall CV score), matching vs. missing skills chips with a tiered severity breakdown, keyword ATS coverage with a progress bar and over-used keyword warnings, seniority alignment narrative, negotiation angle, recruiter risk flags, CV rewrite suggestions, and talking points for the recruiter interview.
contexts.name: job-fit-analysis

contexts.description: Live job posting lifecycle: create, publish, close, and manage campaigns for job openings. Tracks job winnability (estimated hire probability), status transitions, and external job board ingestion. Tenancy tests verify that close and lifecycle-signal operations are workspace-scoped.
contexts.name: job-management

contexts.description: The sourcing-campaign surface for a job: displays the recruiter's active outreach variants (message templates or channel selections) and lets them compare variant performance. JobsCampaignTabVariantCard renders each variant's engagement metrics; jobsCampaignTabLogic owns fetch and selection state; jobsCampaignTabTypes defines the variant and campaign payload shapes.
contexts.name: jobs-campaign-tab

contexts.description: The pre-publish winnability coach that tells recruiters whether a JD will actually fill before sourcing begins: how many candidates pass the gates, which requirement is silently emptying the pipeline, and whether the salary undercuts the market. The coach panel is read-only but can build a deep-link (jobsCoachApply) that pre-stages a loosened-gate or demoted-must-have suggestion in the Library JD editor for the recruiter to confirm. jobsCoachSalary formats the salary band through the shared APP_CURRENCY helper.
contexts.name: jobs-coach-panel

contexts.description: Side-by-side interview comparison for a job's candidate cohort: aggregates structured interview evidence across candidates into a cohort table, with per-finding evidence cards for each criterion. jobsCompareCohorts contains the pure logic that merges raw interview transcripts into normalized, comparable cohort rows; the types module defines the evidence card and cohort table shapes.
contexts.name: jobs-compare-interviews

contexts.description: Handles ad-ingest (parsing a third-party job ad URL into a structured job row) and job posting (publishing a draft job to external channels). JobsIngestAdPanel fetches parse results and shows the field-by-field extraction preview; jobsIngestAdPanelLogic owns the async ingest state machine. JobsPostingModal and its footer let the recruiter review and confirm the post; jobsPostingModalLogic manages the multi-step confirmation flow. JobsDraftsPanel surfaces unpublished drafts waiting for the recruiter's action.
contexts.name: jobs-ingest-posting

contexts.description: Unit tests for the jobs-surface pure logic layer, covering coach-apply deep-link encoding/decoding, coach salary formatting, cohort merge logic, ingest latch deduplication, rediscovery add outcome transitions, request guard validation, status merge correctness, and markdown serialization. All tests are dependency-free TypeScript and serve as the authoritative contract for the shared jobs business rules.
contexts.name: jobs-library-tests

contexts.description: The recruiter's main jobs browse surface: a filterable, sortable table of all jobs with lifecycle status, salary band, role family, and seniority columns. JobsTab orchestrates tab-level state and deep-link routing while JobsTable/JobsRow render the data grid; JobsTabFilters and JobsTabResults handle the filter bar and empty/results copy; useJobsList fetches and refreshes the job list; JobsLifecycleStrip and JobsEmptyLaunchpad cover the lifecycle bar and the zero-state call to action.
contexts.name: jobs-list-view

contexts.name: jobs-recruiter-candidates

contexts.description: Surfaces AI-generated talent rediscovery alerts for a job — previously-seen candidates who have become newly eligible due to updated profiles or loosened requirements. JobsRediscoverPanel is the side-panel entry point that hosts the feed within the jobs detail view.

contexts.name: jobs-shared-logic

contexts.description: The public /about marketing page rendered as a scroll-animated serpentine timeline of the seven pipeline phases (Design → Source → Intake → Screen → Interview → Offer → Hired). contexts.name: landing-brand-mark

contexts.description: Animated product-preview modals triggered by hovering or clicking feature sticker cards on the landing page. Each of the six previews (job-fit score dial, voice screening transcript, self-scheduling calendar, multi-channel inbox, salary radar, and human-gate queue) is a self-contained Framer Motion choreography that replays on every peek. A shared `FeatureSpotlight` wrapper handles the pinned/hover state, Escape key dismissal, and ARIA dialog semantics.
contexts.name: landing-feature-spotlights

Writes the NEXT_LOCALE cookie via the `setLocale` server action then calls `router.refresh()` to re-render under the new locale — the same mechanism as the workspace LanguageSwitcher, styled to match the marketing pages.
contexts.name: landing-lang-switch

contexts.description: Public pricing section rendered as four animated sticker-card tiers (Free, Starter, Growth, BYOM) on an amber band, plus an enterprise contact-sales block with ROI statistics. Self-serve tiers call `enterWorkspace(tierId)` to enter the product; enterprise routes to a sales mailto. All copy — tier names, feature bullets, prices, enterprise capabilities — resolves through the `landing.pricing` i18n namespace.
contexts.name: landing-pricing

contexts.name: landing-spark-tokens

contexts.name: llm-config-secrets

contexts.name: llm-configuration

contexts.api_surface: Internal execution helpers consumed by analysis and devcase run modules

contexts.name: llm-execution

contexts.description: Tracks and meters all LLM call sites: the usage ledger records token counts and dollar costs per operation, LightTrack integration ships observability events to a local tracing proxy, quality scores validate response structure, and ops telemetry emits structured logs for operational monitoring.
contexts.name: llm-observability

contexts.name: llm-provider-layer

Depends on next-intl for translations, the shared TextInput and toast-store primitives, and the /api/auth/login API route.
contexts.name: login-flow

contexts.description: Build pipeline that pulls Czech labour-market data from the external Pumper service (MPSV-VPM + MPSV-ISPV datasets), maps CZ-ISCO occupation codes onto kp's 16 role families, and writes a committed snapshot at data/market_pulse.json consumed by the /market page. contexts.name: market-pulse-builder

contexts.description: The public /market Czech labour-market intelligence page ('Atlas' variant). Data comes from `data/market_pulse.json` (built by the Pumper mpsv-vpm/mpsv-ispv scrapers); the page shell loads Spark fonts and delegates to MarketPulseAtlas for the body.
contexts.name: market-pulse-page

contexts.description: Presentational React components shared by every match surface: score Bar, weight-aware BreakdownBar, NoMatchesNote, and the async ReasoningPanel that shows the 'Explain fit' verdict. Composes on Meter, Badge, and Framer Motion, and collapses motion under the OS reduce-motion preference.
contexts.name: match-presentation-components

contexts.name: match-run-logic

All match features (hiring, library, compare, group-eval) import from here so the score contract and display vocabulary can never silently drift between surfaces.
contexts.name: match-score-shared-types

contexts.description: The Match tab workspace — allows a recruiter to run an AI match between a job (from saved JDs) and a pool of candidates (from profiles or analyses), then view ranked results with skill chips, weight controls, and bulk actions. MatchResults renders the ranked card list; MatchCard shows individual candidate fit; MatchJobCompare and MatchWeightsPanel let the recruiter tune and compare. Results persist via matchResultsWriteback.
contexts.name: match-tab-ui

contexts.name: matrix-logic

contexts.description: The Fit Matrix tab UI: a candidates-×-positions grid where each cell shows the AI match score with colour-coded strength, a popover for on-demand score reasoning, a select-mode for bulk shortlisting to the pipeline, a filter row (role family, min-fit floor), data notices for coverage gaps, and empty/stale-job states. All grid state and handlers are delegated to the useMatrixTab hook; this layer is purely render.
contexts.name: matrix-tab-ui

APP_LANGUAGES is also co-located here as the canonical list of supported locales.
contexts.name: member-ui-helpers

contexts.name: models-api-keys

PATCH actions update llm_config rows via /api/llm/config; modelsRoutingActions contains the server-side action helpers.
contexts.name: models-routing-config

contexts.name: models-usage-quality

Also injects importAttributes for JSON modules. Production builds never load this file.
contexts.name: node-test-infra

contexts.description: Manages the offer lifecycle from drafting through acceptance, decline, and expiry: offer policy rules (approval gates, expiry deadlines), finalization with legal seal, automated reminder cadence, and the offer store. contexts.name: offer-management
