Handles all terminal states (accepted, declined, expired) with accessible live-region announcements and wires the accepted state to the onboarding CTA at /onboarding/[token].
contexts.name: offer-response-page

contexts.description: The Onboarding tab that bridges hired candidates into a structured first-day process: lists candidates ready to onboard (not yet started), shows all active and completed onboarding runs, and exposes empty-state variants (baseline, first-day plan, hand-off record) for prototyping the first-run UX. Manages the template selection that seeds a new run.
contexts.name: onboarding-core

contexts.description: First-run setup wizard for new workspaces: onboarding state machine tracking which setup steps are complete (company profile, relay config, first JD, invite teammates), candidate-side onboarding for new portal users, and intake flow for collecting the minimum required information. Getting-started checklist drives the sidebar progress indicator.
contexts.name: onboarding-flow

Code-split from the tab so the detail chunk is only loaded on click.
contexts.name: onboarding-run-detail

contexts.description: Template management for onboarding runs: a section listing saved templates with an inline create-new affordance, and the full template manager editor (code-split) for editing checklist items, questionnaire fields, and signature slots. Templates are selected at run-start time to seed the run's structure.

Depends on usePipelineTabState for data and on the shared Entry type from pipelineTypes.

contexts.name: pipeline-bulk-actions

contexts.name: pipeline-data-seeding

Scores are merged from the canonical fit-score cache on every read.

contexts.description: Single-sources the canonical TypeScript shapes for pipeline entries, positions, decisions, offer drafts, and candidate profiles so the hiring pipeline, decisions, and candidate-intelligence features share one declaration instead of private copies that could silently drift. Includes Entry (pipeline board), Position (job lane), Screening, Offer, isScoreStale, and the provenance/archetype helpers (matchScoreForPipeline, provLabel, formatBandCompact). Also owns the pure pipelineRematchLink parser that turns re-engagement event details into navigable counterpart references.
contexts.name: pipeline-entry-types

contexts.description: The board's filter bar and toolbar: free-text search, quick-filter chips, score-band facets, source facets, sort control, SLA deadline editor, saved-view dialog, and the board toolbar that hosts these controls. Renders on the first frame regardless of board fetch state and binds to the URL for deep-linkable filter state.
contexts.name: pipeline-filter-toolbar

contexts.description: Cross-cutting UX components that guide recruiters through multi-step hiring-chain workflows. `ChainEmptyState` is shown on any tab whose data depends on an upstream step — it explains what the missing prerequisite is and deep-links to it. `CompletionCta` is a post-mutation success banner with contextual deep-link buttons pointing to where the results landed (e.g., after bulk-adding candidates it links to the Pipeline tab).
contexts.name: pipeline-navigation-ux

contexts.description: Control surface and status display for the durable background automation scheduler that runs AI policy passes on a cadence (Task-7). Shows last-run time, engine availability, run history, reminder delivery counts, and provides a manual trigger. Includes state hook and all sub-panels for the scheduler widget.
contexts.name: pipeline-scheduler

contexts.api_surface: Internal helpers consumed by screening wave and pipeline list
contexts.description: Caches match scores per pipeline entry to avoid redundant AI calls on every page load. Also provides match-input serialisation and candidate match-score resolution — the layer that coerces raw analysis scores into the canonical match format consumed by the pipeline list and screening wave.
contexts.name: pipeline-score-cache

contexts.description: The state machine for candidate pipeline entries: stage enumeration (screening, interview, offer, hired, rejected), status transitions, pipeline commands that trigger moves, and the public event log. Controls what actions are legal at each stage and emits structured events that the comms layer dispatches.
contexts.name: pipeline-status-flow

contexts.description: Unit tests for the pure pipeline business-logic modules: board layout, filter predicates, sort/view serialization, bulk-confirm rules, stage-move target resolution, render-diet aging buckets, and the result-view unpriced edge case. All run under Node with no DOM dependency.
contexts.name: pipeline-tests

contexts.description: Headless, idempotent setup script for the Polar billing integration. Validates the API token, reconciles live product prices against the in-repo catalog, creates any missing one-time credit pack, and ensures exactly one webhook endpoint points at <tunnel>/api/billing/webhook — writing POLAR_WEBHOOK_SECRET to .env so the secret stays stable across dev sessions. Safe to re-run; warns loudly on price drift without modifying existing prices.
contexts.name: polar-billing-setup

contexts.description: The About tab: a static capability browser that documents every kp feature — CV analysis, matching, pipeline automation, voice interview, offer flow, dev-cases, and the early-career thesis — as a navigable catalogue of PlantUML component diagrams and prose. Also hosts the Students sub-section with a worked scoring example and interview thought-script, and links to the guided simulation tour. No data fetches; content is static TypeScript data.
contexts.name: product-capability-browser

contexts.description: The candidate profile creation and editing surface — captures structured competency signals (skills, experience, archetype assignment) via a multi-field form with AI-draft assist. ProfileEditorAiDraft triggers an LLM-assisted pre-fill from an analysis slug; profileEditorPayload assembles the save payload; profileCompletenessFields computes field completeness scores. ProfileForm + ProfileFields define the field schema and validation contract.
contexts.name: profile-editor

contexts.description: The Profile tab shell and its two overview surfaces — the roster (list of all saved profiles with staleness badges) and the candidate matrix (profiles grouped by archetype in a grid cell view). ProfileTab orchestrates deep-link routing between editor, roster, and matrix. useProfileTabDeepLinks resolves URL params to open the editor or highlight a profile. ProfileTabRebuildWarnModal warns when a rebuilt profile will overwrite manual edits.
contexts.name: profile-roster-tab

contexts.description: A fully client-side PlantUML component-diagram renderer with no external server dependency. It parses a PlantUML-subset source string, runs ELK auto-layout, and emits a styled, interactive SVG using the workspace's design tokens. Supports component/database/cloud/actor/folder/note node shapes, container groups, edge labels, status stereotypes (live/gate/todo), and clickable nodes. An expandable full-screen modal with zoom handles dense diagrams. Used on the landing about page and wherever architecture or pipeline-funnel diagrams appear.
contexts.name: puml-diagram-renderer

contexts.description: Mobile-first one-screen lead form (/apply/[id]/quick) designed for paid-traffic and social ad links — captures name, email, and knockout answers in a single tap with sub-30-second completion time. The server page resolves campaign/variant attribution from UTM parameters and checks the job's lifecycle gate; QuickApplyForm is a stateful client component with a honeypot anti-bot field, inline validation, and an enrichment CTA that deep-links the candidate into the full conversational apply with their lead token pre-seeded. Posts to /api/apply/[id]/quick and returns a status token for candidate self-tracking.
contexts.name: quick-apply-flow

contexts.description: Shared React hooks used across recruiter and candidate-facing pages: infinite scroll, JSON fetch with loading state, loader lifecycle, reach-out action trigger, reduced-motion preference, relative timestamp formatting, slot label display, and the add-to-pipeline action hook.
contexts.name: react-hooks

contexts.api_surface: rank_candidates(), fairness_check(), generate_comparison(); CLI: recruiter_cli.py, group_compare_cli.py
contexts.description: Recruiter-facing inverse of matching: scores all candidates against one job and returns a fairness-tracked ranked view (early-career vs experienced on separate tracks). Group comparison generates LLM-synthesized comparative prose with **bold** emphasis for the Decisions group-eval panel. Both modules reuse the production scorers exactly so the coach view and publish view can never disagree.
contexts.name: recruiter-ranking

contexts.description: Salary benchmarking data layer: per-org salary benchmarks for role families (stored in org_benchmarks), market comparison via the salary_benchmarks table seeded from market data, and the confidence-pinned band display logic. Powers the offer compensation guidance in the offers flow.
contexts.name: salary-benchmarks

contexts.description: The salary estimation result tab that presents the AI salary estimate with a visual min/midpoint/max gauge, confidence badge, rounded growth-target callout, grounded market evidence from web search (with sources and methodology notes), and a company-type compensation adjustment factor (startup vs. corporate). The gauge logic is co-located as a pure function to enable deterministic unit testing of range mapping and confidence display.
contexts.name: salary-estimation

contexts.description: Market-aware salary band logic: plausibility ceilings, rounding to market grain, company-type adjustments (startup vs multinational), and an evidence trace that shows the recruiter WHY a salary range was estimated. MarketConfig externalizes all Czech/market-specific constants so re-homing to a new market is config, not code. Mirrors the TypeScript normalizeSalaryBand contract to prevent pipeline/UI drift.
contexts.name: salary-market-intelligence

contexts.description: Handles the Enterprise contact-sales flow: captures the sales contact lead submission and routes it to the configured destination. Used by the pricing page's 'Talk to sales' CTA for the Enterprise contact-sales tier.
contexts.name: sales-contact

contexts.description: Renders the persisted CV analysis report for a specific candidate at /history/[slug]. Loads the stored analysis row from SQLite via loadAnalysis, validates the payload against analysisSchema, enriches it with live board position, cross-job footprint (same cv_hash against other JDs), label-collision warnings, and a JD-staleness badge, then delegates rendering to ResultPanel. All secondary lookups are best-effort — store faults hide the enrichment chip rather than crashing the page.
contexts.name: saved-analysis-report

contexts.description: The interactive weekly calendar grid where recruiters pick interview slots for candidates. The week pager navigates forward and back; each cell shows availability and booked markers; slot-part helpers compute the grid positioning. Add-to-calendar links and meeting link cells give candidates the joining details.
contexts.name: schedule-calendar

contexts.description: The interview prep modal that gives the recruiter a structured run-of-show, AI-generated question suggestions, and note-taking space before the interview starts. The useScheduleInterviewPrep hook fetches and caches the prep pack per candidate; load-state components handle the async fetch gracefully.
contexts.name: schedule-interview-prep

contexts.description: Post-interview review surfaces: transcript viewer (turn-by-turn conversation replay), AI scorecard section (model-generated rating), human scorecard form and panel (recruiter ratings), telemetry strip (duration, WER, latency), and scorecard row primitives. The transcript-helpers module parses raw transcript data for display.
contexts.name: schedule-interview-review

contexts.description: Tracks the full lifecycle of a scheduling invite from sent to confirmed to stalled: a panel that shows confirmed bookings, attention items (stalled or drifted invites), and invite history. The lifecycle hook computes which bucket each invite is in; the popover dismiss hook handles tooltip persistence.
contexts.name: schedule-invite-lifecycle

contexts.description: The Schedule tab shell that orchestrates the calendar grid, the pending-to-interview list, and the already-interviewed list within a two-column layout. Manages the empty relay state (showing the Decisions → Schedule → Interview flow when nothing is ready), and renders the interview prep and transcript modals via code-split dynamic imports.
contexts.name: schedule-tab-layout

contexts.description: Unit tests for the scheduling business-logic modules: lifecycle-bucket computation (which bucket an invite falls into by age and status) and popover-dismiss persistence logic.
contexts.name: schedule-tests

contexts.description: Core types and state hook for the Schedule tab: SchedEntry shape, slot grammar (dated ISO format), the useScheduleTab hook that fetches entries, manages picks, derives calendar and interviewed lists, and fires slot confirmation actions. The slot-label formatter localizes the ISO date grammar for display.
contexts.name: schedule-types-and-state

contexts.description: Manages interview and meeting scheduling: slot availability resolution, calendar link generation (Google/Outlook/ical), appointment booking with conflict detection, a persistent schedule store, and a scheduler health monitor. Powers the self-scheduling candidate experience where candidates pick their own interview slot.
contexts.name: scheduling-calendar

contexts.description: Generates TypeScript artifacts from Python as the single source of truth: exports AnalysisResult JSON Schema as Zod definitions to app/_lib/schemas.generated.ts, and exports evidence/skill/provenance enums to app/_lib/taxonomy.generated.ts. Run via `python -m pipeline.jobfit.codegen`; `--check` mode fails CI if the generated files drift from the Python source.
contexts.name: schema-codegen

contexts.description: The shared visual vocabulary for communicating AI-derived candidate quality scores throughout the recruiter workspace. `ScoreDial` renders an animated arc with a count-up number; `ScoreBadge` is a compact inline score chip with band label; `ScoreProvenanceLabel` indicates how a score was derived (AI vs. manual); `Meter` is a theme-coded progress bar used for sub-scores. All scoring logic is co-located in pure functions to enable unit testing independent of React.
contexts.name: score-display-primitives

contexts.description: The persistent Getting Started checklist shown in the sidebar rail after the setup wizard completes. Surfaces the next recommended action (SetupGettingStartedNextMove), individual rail-embedded step indicators (SetupGettingStartedRailStep), and the collapsible card (GettingStartedCard) that lets users track and dismiss post-setup checklist items.
contexts.name: setup-getting-started

contexts.description: The first-run setup wizard that fires when a new tenant lands at / for the first time. A five-step branded takeover (Welcome → Company → Team → First role → Handoff) guides an admin through configuring the workspace; each step maps to a step component and a data model. POST /api/me/onboarding persists completion so the gate never re-fires.
contexts.name: setup-onboarding-wizard

contexts.description: Common scaffolding for all Python CLIs spawned by Next.js API routes: UTF-8 stdio configuration for Windows cp1250 compatibility, MatchCandidate/Job argument loading helpers, and the JSON error envelope contract. logger.py provides StageTimer and append_pipeline_log for structured per-stage timing logs. cli.py and extract_cli.py are the top-level service entry points.
contexts.name: shared-cli-scaffolding

contexts.api_surface: Browser-safe pure helpers, no API surface
contexts.description: Stateless pure utility functions used across the entire app: locale-aware date/number formatting, deduplication helpers, cryptographically random ID generation, safe URL validation, initials extraction, list splitting, CSV export utils, URL param encoding, and the public base URL resolver.
contexts.name: shared-primitives

contexts.description: The global Ctrl/Cmd+K command palette that searches candidates, pipeline entries, jobs, and saved analyses via /api/search while also listing all nav tabs as instant actions. Results are ranked and deduplicated through workspacePaletteResults; keyboard navigation and recents integration are wired in the Modal overlay.
contexts.name: shell-command-palette

contexts.description: The 'g-chord' keyboard navigation layer and '?' shortcuts reference overlay for the workspace. Chord sequences (g→p for Pipeline, g→c for Channels, etc.) are derived declaratively from NAV_GROUPS so adding a tab automatically gains a shortcut without touching this module.
contexts.name: shell-keyboard-shortcuts

contexts.description: A thin event-bus that lets any mutating fetch signal all open views to re-load their data. Cross-window refresh is implemented via BroadcastChannel so a mutation in one browser tab (e.g. the pipeline board) refreshes a simultaneously open decisions view in another. useAttention polls /api/attention every 60 s and subscribes to this bus to keep nav-badge counts current.
contexts.name: shell-live-refresh

contexts.description: Tracks recently visited candidates, jobs, and pipeline entries in sessionStorage so the command palette can surface them instantly before a search query is typed. RecordRecent is a lightweight client component that writes a visit on mount; WorkspaceRecentsNav renders the resulting list.
contexts.name: shell-recents

contexts.description: The two-level icon-rail + item-panel sidebar that lets users switch between all workspace tabs. Handles both the desktop permanent rail (md+) and the mobile off-canvas drawer including focus-trap, inert marking, and auto-close on navigation. Houses per-section glyph metadata, the brand-mark, and the appearance/language preferences footer tile.
contexts.name: shell-sidebar-navigation

contexts.description: The top-level Workspace component that stitches together the sidebar, tab panel, and all shell providers. It owns tab-identity routing (WorkspaceTabId union, URL construction, deep-link param clearing), the mobile-drawer breakpoint tracker, and the first-run onboarding gate. Depends on TasksProvider and SimulationProvider as context roots.
contexts.name: shell-workspace-container

contexts.description: All UI surfaces that drive and display the pipeline simulation: the persistent bottom SimBar with play/pause/reset controls, the dual-face SimControlDock (Ops overview + live Sim face), spotlight annotations, decision wave overlays, group-eval modal, offer frame, and the explain drawer. Consumes SimCtx from SimulationProvider and renders no business data of its own.
contexts.name: simulation-control-ui

contexts.description: The state machine and scripted walk engine powering the guided JD→Hired pipeline demo. SimulationProvider maintains run/pause/stop lifecycle and exposes SimCtx to all surfaces; useSimulationWalk sequences phase steps with paced beats; useSimulationEngine applies mutations. Scenario data (company templates, criteria, diagrams, phase steps) lives in the sibling data files.
contexts.name: simulation-engine

contexts.description: Token-gated public Skill Profile page (/skill/[token]) that renders a candidate-owned, shareable score-card credential. Verifies the token server-side via verifySkillProfileToken, computes freshness and state (verified/stale/tampered/revoked/incomplete/unverifiable), and presents durable skill axes with transfer score, confidence, and a tamper-evident shield badge. Depends on app/_lib/skill-profile and app/_lib/db for token verification, and next-intl for localization.
contexts.name: skill-profile-public-page

contexts.description: The canonical skill/role/company taxonomy: a JSON-backed graph of role families, skill synonyms, seniority signals, company-type classifiers, and language aliases. Normalization, fuzzy resolution, and provenance-weighted skill match scoring live here. i18n.py handles locale routing (EN/CS) for prompts and output. taxonomy_check.py audits the graph for consistency.
contexts.name: skill-taxonomy

contexts.description: Generates social-sourcing campaign packs for a published job: 6-12 feed-ready ad-copy variants and 15-second vertical video scripts following the 4-beat formula (hook → role+offer → proof → CTA). Honesty-gated: only stated job facts appear in copy; assumed/defaulted values (phantom location, salary) are never advertised. Uses ClaudeCliProvider with a deterministic fallback.
contexts.name: sourcing-campaign

contexts.description: The primary public-facing marketing homepage ('Spark' art direction — sticker-sheet maximalism with ink outlines, rotated cards, and offset shadows). Renders the hero with interactive stamped CV cards, a marquee, a three-step how-it-works section, a feature sticker grid, a voice-interview teaser, a responsible-AI compliance section, a pricing block, and a closing CTA. All visible copy is served through the `landing` i18n namespace; only layout constants (colors, icon picks, rotation angles) live in the component.
contexts.name: spark-landing-home

contexts.description: Candidate discovery and silver-medalist rediscovery: list and filter candidates for a job, trigger recruiter-CLI outreach campaigns, and run/refresh the rediscovery-alert feed that surfaces past candidates who fit newly opened roles. Sweep tenancy tests confirm that alert writes and reads stay within the calling workspace.
contexts.name: talent-sourcing

contexts.api_surface: Consumed by every API route that accepts or returns analysis payloads
contexts.description: Machine-readable taxonomy of roles, skill families, archetypes, and the Zod schemas that validate analysis result payloads. The generated files (schemas.generated.ts, taxonomy.generated.ts) are produced by the Python pipeline and kept in-tree so TypeScript consumers don't depend on a runtime build step.
contexts.name: taxonomy-schemas

contexts.description: Machine-checked manifest of which database tables are workspace-scoped. Maintains an explicit allowlist of VERIFIED-scoped tables and EXEMPT globals, enabling a boot-time assertion that every persistent table is either scoped or consciously exempted — fail-closed so new tables cannot silently re-open cross-tenant data leaks.
contexts.name: tenancy-isolation

contexts.description: Test-only infrastructure: an in-memory SQLite unit-db fixture that seeds isolated schema instances for fast unit tests without hitting the real file, and sanity checks that run on import to catch configuration mistakes at startup. The DB test isolation guard verifies tests don't share mutable state.
contexts.name: testing-infra

contexts.description: Test suite for pipeline automation tasks, campaign generation, interview evaluation, voice harness, and the registry/job/seed shared layer. Covers automation task execution, automation CLI, automation eval quality, campaign pack generation, interview evaluation and rubrics, interview scenario mapping, voice harness smoke tests, job loading, and seed candidates.
contexts.name: tests-automation-pipeline

contexts.description: Test suite for candidate profiling, archetype detection, soft signals, and transferable skill mapping. Covers v2 profile building, profile CLIs, profile/taxonomy contract, profiling utilities, early-career single-source enforcement, soft signal panel, transferable mapping, and transform logic.
contexts.name: tests-candidate-profile

contexts.description: Test suite for CV text extraction, multimodal Gemini analysis, PII redaction, and authenticity/credential trust checks. Covers extractors, Gemini metering/oversize/truncation edge cases, PDF parsing quality, credential expiry detection, blind-screening redaction, and authenticity heuristics.
contexts.name: tests-cv-extraction

contexts.description: Test suite for the CV analysis pipeline, ATS keyword coverage, prompt versioning, and analysis honesty. Covers pipeline orchestration, graceful degradation (degrade tests), pipeline diagram contract, prompt version synchronization, CSAS alignment, and analysis-result honesty fields.
contexts.name: tests-cv-scoring

contexts.description: Test suite for the developer assessment pipeline: all devcase stages (analyze, design, evaluate, reflect, calibrate), anti-cheat controls (provenance, artifact checks), scenario generation, lifecycle and submission evaluation, LLM judge independence, live-case integration, and seed materialization.
contexts.name: tests-devcase

contexts.description: Test suite for the multi-LLM infrastructure: provider base class, registry resolution, offline mode, monitor, LLM benchmark (bake quality, bench), BYOM coverage, graded fallback behavior, self-hosted model support, prompt budget enforcement, and Claude CLI provider.
contexts.name: tests-llm-infra

contexts.description: Test suite for the candidate matching engine, recruiter ranking, group comparison, and JD winnability. Covers KO filter logic, score sanity, scoring contract, match reasoning, matched provenance honesty, matrix CLI, hotpath deduplication, scorecard notes, weight proposals, and winnability assessment.
contexts.name: tests-matching-scoring

contexts.description: Test suite for salary logic, market configuration, fairness, and compliance: salary band normalization, currency validation, salary sanity ranges, market config correctness, insights evidence, calibration drift detection, fairness matrix, name neutrality, false skill credit prevention, unproven skill boundary enforcement, and sibling skill credit.
contexts.name: tests-salary-compliance

contexts.description: Test suite for the skill and role taxonomy: graph consistency, coverage gates, role family routing and parity, tech bilingual parity (EN/CS skill names), whole-token classification, and non-tech skill graph correctness.
contexts.name: tests-skill-taxonomy

contexts.description: Core behavioral UI primitives that every workspace surface depends on: modal dialogs with focus trapping, route-level error and loading fallbacks, skeleton placeholder tiles, a toast notification system with a persistent Zustand-like store, and a Markdown-to-safe-HTML renderer for LLM-generated content. These are the lowest-level interactive building blocks above raw HTML.
contexts.name: ui-primitives

contexts.description: The single-source Tailwind class-string recipe library and UI infrastructure primitives. `recipes.ts` defines named class constants (PANEL, BTN_PRIMARY, CHIP, FIELD, EYEBROW, etc.) consumed by 90+ surfaces to prevent token drift across themes. `Defer.tsx` is a performance primitive that delays heavy subtree mounts using idle/next-frame/visible strategies. `useTheme` and `SectionTitle` handle theme-aware rendering.
contexts.name: ui-token-recipes

contexts.description: Provider-agnostic voice adapter layer with concrete implementations for OpenAI Realtime and ElevenLabs. Exposes a unified VoiceAdapter interface for connecting, sending audio turns, and retrieving transcripts. Includes self-hosted provider detection (on-premise Piper TTS / ElevenLabs proxy) and failover logic when the primary provider is unavailable.
contexts.name: voice-adapters

contexts.description: Audio-in-the-loop evaluation harness for the voice interview feature: local Piper TTS speaks candidate answers into the real ElevenLabs Realtime WebSocket, wer.py measures Word Error Rate, and session_runner.py orchestrates full interview sessions. elevenlabs_backend.py is the Python-side ElevenLabs adapter mirroring the TS runtime adapter. v0_smoke.py proved the protocol (WER 0.00%) with 3 hard-won protocol fixes.
contexts.name: voice-eval-harness

contexts.api_surface: GET/POST /api/interview/connect, POST /api/interview/create, POST /api/interview/complete, POST /api/interview/revoke, GET /api/interview/by-entry, GET /api/interview/compare
contexts.description: Real-time AI voice interview management: mints short-lived browser credentials for OpenAI Realtime or ElevenLabs, creates and loads interview sessions linked to pipeline entries, and marks completion with usage attribution. Supports provider failover, consent gating, rate limiting, and post-interview comparison of multiple sessions.
contexts.name: voice-interview

contexts.description: Developer scripts for configuring and testing the voice interview subsystem. setup-eleven-agent.mjs idempotently creates or updates the ElevenLabs Conversational AI agent (voice selection, ASR keyword biasing, per-candidate override enablement) and writes ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID back to .env.local. interview-brief.ts and interview-brief-grounded.ts emit the exact production interviewer briefs to stdout so the Python eval harness can test real prompts headlessly without a running server.
contexts.name: voice-interview-dev-tools

contexts.description: The live AI voice interview browser interface. `VoiceInterview` connects to either OpenAI Realtime (WebRTC) or ElevenLabs Agents (WebSocket SDK), streams a live transcript, handles mic/audio mute, shows an elapsed timer and speaking/listening status pill, runs a pre-call mic test, and on hang-up POSTs the full transcript to `/api/interview/complete` for scoring with retry and `sendBeacon` fallback. `VoiceInterviewClient` wraps it in a dynamic SSR-skipping import since WebRTC/AudioContext are browser-only. `InterviewSidebar` is the candidate-facing rail showing the interview agenda, estimated duration, and pre-interview readiness tips.
contexts.name: voice-interview-ui

contexts.description: Manages the voice interview session lifecycle: generating the candidate brief prompt, locking the session to a single language, computing per-minute pricing for billing, finalizing session status (completed/abandoned/error), and formatting telemetry events for the session transcript store. Wraps the provider-level connection in the recruiter-facing interview lab.
contexts.name: voice-session-flow

contexts.description: Lists all workspaces for the current user, creates new ones, and switches the active session workspace via /api/auth/switch-workspace. A tenancy gate (multiWorkspace flag) hides the create/switch UI until per-workspace data isolation is enforced, preventing a premature action from leaking cross-tenant data; the banner explains why the feature is locked.
contexts.name: workspace-admin

contexts.description: SVG illustration data modules for the 14 primary workspace feature areas: Pipeline, Analytics, Decisions, Schedule, Jobs, Library, Developer Cases, Matrix, Profile Matrix, Profile Roster, and the four sourcing channel types (Ads, Careers, Comms, Email). Each exports a `{ viewBox, data }` object consumed by `MotionizedGlyph` to render as a self-drawing empty-state illustration. These provide the visual identity for feature empty states throughout the recruiter workspace.
contexts.name: workspace-feature-glyphs

contexts.api_surface: GET/PUT /api/brand, GET /api/compliance, GET/DELETE /api/data/[token], GET /api/health, GET /api/ops, POST /api/demo
contexts.description: Workspace configuration and compliance: brand settings (logo, colors), the active GDPR/legal compliance regime, and the public GDPR data self-service endpoint (right-to-erasure, right-to-access) exposed via opaque erasure tokens in candidate communications. Health probe and ops dashboard give operators a live read of DB, engine, comms, and scheduler health; demo mode toggle and upload-size contract are also housed here.
contexts.name: workspace-settings

contexts.description: The three persistent controls that live in the sidebar rail footer: the Studio Light / Spark Dark theme toggle, the locale switcher (language selector), and the sign-out button. The sign-out button calls `leaveWorkspace()` which POSTs `/api/auth/logout` (clears the `__Host-kp_session` cookie) and hard-navigates to the landing page — it is the only UI path that fully ends a workspace session.
contexts.name: workspace-sidebar-controls

use_cases.description: A candidate receives a tokenized link, joins a browser-based session, and completes a first-round AI voice interview; the platform transcribes, scores, and stores the outcome for the recruiter.
use_cases.name: AI Voice Screening

use_cases.description: A recruiter fills a brief form; the platform generates a structured, localized job description in the background and scores it for winnability via the coach panel before publishing.
use_cases.name: AI-Assisted JD Authoring

use_cases.description: When a candidate is accepted, the platform pushes a structured candidate record to the configured external ATS (Recruitis, Teamio, or webhook), closing the loop with systems the buyer already depends on.
use_cases.name: ATS Candidate Egress

use_cases.description: A recruiter uploads one or more CVs (optionally pairing them with a JD), the platform runs a multi-phase AI analysis, and returns a scored report covering job-fit, salary estimate, interview prep, and GitHub evidence.
use_cases.name: CV Analysis Pipeline

use_cases.description: A job seeker discovers an open role and applies via standard form, mobile quick-apply, or a conversational chat flow; the platform deduplicates, scores KO questions, and places them into the pipeline.
use_cases.name: Candidate Application Intake

use_cases.description: Recruiters move candidates across Kanban stages (screening → interview → offer → hired/rejected), apply bulk actions, set SLA deadlines, and view AI scores — all from a single board.
use_cases.name: Candidate Pipeline Board

use_cases.description: After advancing in the pipeline, a candidate receives a tokenized invite link, browses available slots, and confirms an interview time without recruiter involvement.
use_cases.name: Candidate Self-Scheduling

use_cases.description: The platform scores a pool of candidate profiles against a job description and renders a ranked matrix so recruiters can instantly see fit, skill gaps, and KO reasons across all applicants.
use_cases.name: Candidate–Job Matching

use_cases.description: Every AI-driven accept/reject passes through a human-in-the-loop queue, is sealed with an Art. 22 compliance tier, and is written to an immutable audit log — satisfying EU AI Act obligations.
use_cases.name: Compliant Hiring Decision

use_cases.description: A recruiter designs a seed-based coding challenge, a candidate completes it in the in-browser live workspace, and the platform evaluates the submission for authenticity and quality.
use_cases.name: Developer Case Assessment

use_cases.description: A recruiter drafts an offer with approval gates and legal clauses, sends it to the candidate, who accepts or declines via a tokenized page; the accepted hire then flows into onboarding.
use_cases.name: Offer Lifecycle Management

use_cases.description: Recruiters and managers view stage-by-stage conversion, time-to-hire, channel ROI, automation impact, and AI cost-per-hire across configurable time windows.
use_cases.name: Recruitment Funnel Analytics
